title: Supervision and Regulation
summary: This Federal Reserve Annual Report chapter describes the supervisory and regulatory framework for U.S. banking organizations as of year-end 2024, detailing the portfolio categories used to organize supervised institutions, the number and total assets of banks in each category, and the structure of the Federal Reserve's supervisory approach. The document provides institutional reference data rather than current market-moving information.
key_points: As of December 31, 2024, there were 3,408 community banking organizations with $3.0 trillion in total assets
The LISCC portfolio (8 U.S. G-SIBs) held $15.2 trillion in total assets, representing the largest supervised segment
Large banking organizations (non-LISCC U.S. firms with $100B+ assets) totaled 18 firms with $5.1 trillion in assets
Bank holding companies controlled approximately 95% of all insured commercial bank assets in the United States
Five supervised insurance organizations held approximately $450 billion in total assets as of December 31, 2024
The Federal Reserve supervises financial market utilities (FMUs) designated as systemically important under Dodd-Frank title VIII
